1.title: Directing a Project in Context
1.text: Welcome to Module eleven: Directing a Project in Context. It covers the exam area The prince two processes. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. four point two.one carry out directing a project: activities, inputs and outputs. Recommended roles and responsibilities. How the practices are applied. four point two.two analyze whether the activities, roles and responsibilities are effective and fit for purpose, using the purpose and objectives, the practices and tailoring. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The prince two processes (thirty percent). Exam format: an open-book scenario exam: one hundred fifty minutes, seventy marks, forty-two marks to pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Practitioner syllabus (people cert), version seven point two.

1.title: Purpose, objectives and context
1.text: Purpose, objectives and context. The directing a project process lets the project board be accountable for the project's success. The board makes the key decisions and keeps overall control, and it delegates day-to-day management to the project manager. The process runs from the end of start-up until closure. It is not a stage and not a single event.

1.title: Purpose, objectives and context, continued
1.text: Purpose, objectives and context. The figure shows this: Directing a project: the board's decisions at initiation, project authorization, each stage, ad hoc direction and closure, with management by exception between them.

1.title: Purpose, objectives and context, continued
1.text: Purpose, objectives and context. In plain words, the objectives are. Authority to initiate, deliver and close is given at the right points. The board has the information it needs and control at every decision point. Management gets timely direction and advice when it asks. Closure is authorized and follow-on actions are arranged. The process serves manage by exception (the board steps in only at decision points or on an exception), manage by stages, ensure continued business justification, define roles, responsibilities and relationships and tailor to suit the project. Exam tip: Directing is the board's process and it spans the whole project. The project manager does not direct; the project manager manages within the limits the board sets.

1.title: The board's decisions, inputs and outputs
1.text: The board's decisions, inputs and outputs. The decision names below are in general terms. Learn what the board decides and with which products. Authorize initiation. The board mainly uses: Project brief; initiation stage plan. The board gives: Authority to initiate the project. Authorize the project. The board mainly uses: P I D; plan for the next stage. The board gives: Authority to deliver; baselines accepted; resources committed. Authorize a stage or exception plan. The board mainly uses: End stage report; next stage plan, or exception report and exception plan. The board gives: Authority for the stage, with its tolerances.

1.title: The board's decisions, inputs and outputs, continued
1.text: The board's decisions, inputs and outputs. Give ad hoc direction. The board mainly uses: Highlight reports; issue reports; requests for advice; outside events. The board gives: Decisions and guidance for the project manager. Authorize project closure. The board mainly uses: End project report; lessons report; evidence of acceptance; follow-on action recommendations. The board gives: Closure authorized and follow-on actions accepted.

1.title: The board's decisions, inputs and outputs, continued
1.text: The board's decisions, inputs and outputs. Between these points the board manages by exception. The project manager works within the stage tolerances, and the board reads highlight reports and acts when asked or when an exception is reported. The board can also decide to close the project early if it is no longer justified. Exam tip: Work in a stage starts only when the board has authorized the stage. If a project manager starts the next stage before the board's decision, the approach is not appropriate.

1.title: Roles and responsibilities
1.text: Roles and responsibilities. The board is a team, but one person is accountable overall. Learn each focus and check the Official Book's responsibility table. Executive. Accountable for the project; chairs the board; owns the business case and its continued justification. Senior user. Makes sure the products meet user needs; commits user resources; answers for benefits. Senior supplier. Commits supplier resources; answers for the quality and feasibility of supplier work. Project manager. Supports the board with information, plans and requests for decisions; does not take board decisions.

1.title: Roles and responsibilities, continued
1.text: Roles and responsibilities. Project assurance. Gives the board independent checks, so decisions rest on reliable information. Project support. Administers board papers, meetings and records. Change authority. Decides on changes within delegated limits, so the board does not have to. Corporate or programme management. Sets the project tolerances; receives escalation beyond them. Exam tip: The executive is accountable; the three board roles decide together; the project manager informs but does not decide for the board. In a "who" question, an answer that moves a board decision to the project manager or to assurance is wrong.

1.title: How the practices are applied
1.text: How the practices are applied. Business case. Checks justification at every decision point; stops the project if it no longer holds. Organization. Board in place with all three interests; authority delegated to the project manager. Plans. Approves the project plan baseline and each stage plan; asks for an exception plan when needed. Quality. Satisfied that the quality approach is sound; confirms acceptance at closure.

1.title: How the practices are applied, continued
1.text: How the practices are applied. Risk. Approves the risk approach; takes risks escalated to it. Issues. Decides issues beyond the project manager's authority; sets up the change authority and any change budget. Progress. Sets stage tolerances; reads highlight reports; responds to exception reports. Exam tip: The board delegates by tolerance. Anything the project manager can decide within the stage tolerances should not be brought to the board.

1.title: Judging the process
1.text: Judging the process. Decisions at the right points, with enough information. Next stage approved with no business case review (business justification). Routine work delegated within tolerances. The board approves minor day-to-day choices (manage by exception). Ad hoc direction given quickly when asked. Board members unavailable, so work waits for weeks (manage by stages). The board does not manage the stage. The board gives instructions to team members (define roles).

1.title: Judging the process, continued
1.text: Judging the process. All three interests have a voice. The executive decides alone, or the supplier dominates (define roles). The board stops an unjustified project. Work continues to avoid embarrassment (business justification). Independent information supports decisions. The board relies only on the project manager's view (define roles).

2.title: Judging the process, continued
2.text: Judging the process. Tailoring changes how the board works, not what it decides. Small project. A short board; decisions by email or a brief call; roles combined only where independence and accountability stay clear. Agile or hybrid delivery. The board authorizes stages or releases; the product owner can speak for the user interest; sprints are managed inside the stage. Large or multi-party project. Formal minutes and tighter links with the corporate or programme level. Sustainability and digital concerns. Sustainability targets reviewed at decisions; electronic sign-off and shared dashboards. Exam tip: If a board decides too little, projects drift; if it decides too much, it stops managing by exception. Look for a board that decides at decision points, delegates the rest and answers quickly when asked.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. During Project Harbor's build stage, which is within tolerance, Sam Okafor, the project manager, asks the board to approve swapping two developers between work packages. Was this an appropriate action, and why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: No, because Sam can decide this within the stage tolerances and keep the board for exceptions. Manage by exception means the project manager decides routine matters within tolerance, and the change authority deals with changes to baselines, not resource swaps.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Sam has finished the end stage report and the next stage plan for Project Harbor's pilot stage, and Aisha Bello has checked them. Who makes the decision to authorize the rollout stage? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: The project board, meeting at the stage boundary. The board authorizes each stage, while the project manager and project assurance provide and check the information.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. At the end of Project Harbor's initiation stage, the board must decide whether to authorize the project. Which products does it mainly use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: The P I D and the plan for the first delivery stage. Authorizing the project rests on the P I D and the next stage plan, while the brief and initiation stage plan support the earlier decision to initiate.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Tomas Reyes, the senior user, cannot attend the board meeting that decides on Project Harbor's rollout stage next week and has nominated nobody. What should Sam do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Raise the gap with Marta Quinn so someone with authority covers the user role. The user interest must be represented with authority at the decision, and the project manager cannot take the board's decision or fill the role alone.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. A small internal Brightwater project has a board of three that meets at each stage end and reads a short highlight report by email between meetings. Was this an appropriate way to direct the project, and why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Yes, because the board kept its decision points and used light controls between them. Tailoring lightens the board's working methods while keeping its decisions at the decision points and management by exception between them.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. Delta Software delivers Project Harbor's build stage in two-week sprints. Marta Quinn asks Sam to bring each sprint plan to a board meeting for approval. Was this an appropriate action, and why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: No, because the board authorizes the stage and leaves sprints to the project manager. The board authorizes the stage and sets tolerances, while sprint planning sits inside the stage under the project manager's authority.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the purpose of directing a project? Answer: To let the board be accountable by making key decisions and keeping overall control while delegating day-to-day management to the project manager. Question two. Name the board's five main decisions. Answer: Authorize initiation, authorize the project, authorize a stage or exception plan, give ad hoc direction and authorize project closure. Question three. Who is ultimately accountable on the project board? Answer: The executive.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does manage by exception mean for the board between decision points? Answer: The board lets the project manager work within tolerances and acts on highlight and exception reports. Question five. Which report prompts the board to consider asking for an exception plan? Answer: The exception report. Question six. When does directing a project run? Answer: From the end of start-up until closure.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Purpose: board accountable; key decisions and overall control; day-to-day delegated. Decisions: initiation, the project, a stage or exception plan, ad hoc direction, closure. Inputs: brief, P I D, stage plans, reports, closure information. Roles: executive accountable; senior user and senior supplier; project manager informs. Between decisions: manage by exception within stage tolerances. Red flags: too much detail, slow decisions, a board that manages the stage. Tailoring: lighter methods, same decisions.
